anomalies.observed: C6 is a 100u capacitor drawn in the PWM1 jumper network, in series between the PWM1_C2 wire and the R11 0 Ω jumper. The other jumper paths (R9, R11 for PWM1; R10, R12 for PWM2) are 0 Ω links, and no capacitor appears in the PWM2 network.
anomalies.expected: The spec defines R9–R12 as 0 Ω jumpers that select which M5Stack bus pin (19/21 for ch.1, 20/22 for ch.2) supplies PWM1/PWM2. A 100 µF capacitor in that path would not pass a short. It would block the DC/low-frequency PWM signal from the core to J3 pin 3, so channel 1 could not drive the servo.

evidence.quote: C6 100u with R11 0 in the PWM1_C1/PWM1_C2 jumper block, and "Short R10, R10 for Core2 and CoreS3 / Short R9, R11 for others" (schematic sheet 1/1, upper right)
R9–R12 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | Select which M5Stack bus pin (pin 19/21 for ch.1, pin 20/22 for ch.2) supplies PWM1/PWM2

anomalies.impact: PWM channel 1 (J3 pin 3) would be AC-coupled through a 100 µF capacitor and would not reliably pass the servo control signal. Pan-servo control in PWM mode would fail.

parsed.summary: The schematic places a 100 µF capacitor (C6) in series in the PWM1 jumper path, where the specification calls for a 0 Ω jumper, which would block the PWM1 control signal to the first servo. The rest of the drawing is consistent with the spec at the level of detail visible.
